dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: A local definition taking an implicit type Ω with a measurable-space structure, a measure μ on Ω, and a real-valued function X : Ω → ℝ, and returning the real number `∫ ω, X ω ∂μ`, i.e. the Bochner integral of X with respect to μ. Under a probability measure this is the expectation E[X]. Note it is a total function: for non-integrable X the Bochner integral is defined to be 0 by Mathlib convention, so LocalDef001 μ X is 0 in that case rather than undefined.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the 'expectation' operator appearing on the left of the first conclusion, inside the centering subtraction (X ω − LocalDef001 μ X), and as the outer operator in the second conclusion. The first conjunct asserts precisely that this operator agrees with the Bochner integral of X (which is definitionally trivial given the body).

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: A local definition with the same signature (Ω, measurable space, measure μ, X : Ω → ℝ) → ℝ, defined as LocalDef001 μ (fun ω => (X ω − LocalDef001 μ X)^2), i.e. the integral with respect to μ of the squared deviation of X from its own integral. Under a probability measure this is the variance Var[X] = E[(X − E X)^2]. It is likewise total, inheriting the 'integral of a non-integrable function is 0' convention.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the left-hand side of the second conclusion's equality; that equality states that this 'variance' operator equals the expectation of the squared centered variable — again definitionally true from its body.

binders: Ω : Type (universe u_1), implicit — the underlying sample space
[inst : MeasurableSpace Ω] — instance-implicit σ-algebra on Ω
μ : MeasureTheory.Measure Ω, explicit — a measure on Ω
[MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μ] — instance-implicit assumption that μ is a probability measure (μ(Ω) = 1)
X : Ω → ℝ, explicit — an arbitrary real-valued function (random variable) on Ω, with no measurability assumed at the binder level
No further quantifiers: both statements are implications about this fixed μ and X
hypotheses: Global standing hypotheses: Ω is a measurable space and μ is a probability measure on it; X : Ω → ℝ is arbitrary.
Antecedent of the first implication: MeasureTheory.Integrable X μ, i.e. X is a.e. strongly measurable and has finite integral — X ∈ L¹(μ).
Antecedent of the second implication: MeasureTheory.MemLp X 2 μ, i.e. X is a.e. strongly measurable and its L² seminorm is finite — X ∈ L²(μ), X is square-integrable.
No relation is assumed between the two implications; each carries only its own antecedent.
conclusions: First conjunct (under X ∈ L¹(μ)): LocalDef001 μ X = ∫ ω, X ω ∂μ, i.e. the defined expectation operator applied to X equals the Bochner integral of X with respect to μ. Written mathematically: E[X] = ∫_Ω X dμ.

Second conjunct (under X ∈ L²(μ)), part (a): the function ω ↦ (X ω − LocalDef001 μ X)^2 is Integrable with respect to μ; that is, the squared deviation of X from its expectation is μ-integrable, (X − E X)^2 ∈ L¹(μ).

Second conjunct (under X ∈ L²(μ)), part (b): LocalDef002 μ X = LocalDef001 μ (fun ω ↦ (X ω − LocalDef001 μ X)^2), i.e. the defined variance operator applied to X equals the expectation of the squared centered variable. Written mathematically: Var[X] = E[(X − E[X])^2].
The whole statement is the conjunction: (X ∈ L¹(μ) → E[X] = ∫ X dμ) ∧ (X ∈ L²(μ) → ((X − E X)^2 ∈ L¹(μ) ∧ Var[X] = E[(X − E X)^2])).
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 μ X := ∫ ω, X ω ∂μ — the Bochner integral of X against μ; under a probability measure this is the expectation E[X]. It is a total function of X: by the Mathlib convention the Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0, so LocalDef001 μ X = 0 whenever X is not integrable.

LocalDef002 μ X := LocalDef001 μ (fun ω ↦ (X ω − LocalDef001 μ X)^2) = ∫ ω, (X ω − ∫ X dμ)^2 ∂μ — the variance of X, defined as the expectation of the squared deviation from the mean, again with the junk-value-0 convention when the squared centered function is not integrable.
MeasureTheory.Integrable f μ := AEStronglyMeasurable f μ ∧ HasFiniteIntegral f μ (membership in L¹).
MeasureTheory.MemLp f p μ := AEStronglyMeasurable f μ ∧ eLpNorm f p μ < ∞ (membership in L^p); here p = 2 : ℝ≥0∞.
The exponent 2 in the square is a natural-number exponent interpreted via the monoid power on ℝ (repeated multiplication); the exponent 2 in MemLp is the ENNReal numeral 2.
translation.proposition_plain_english: Let (Ω, F) be a measurable space, let μ be a probability measure on it, and let X : Ω → ℝ be any real-valued function. Define the mean operator E[X] := ∫_Ω X dμ and the variance operator Var[X] := ∫_Ω (X − E[X])^2 dμ. The statement asserts two things at once. First: if X is μ-integrable (X ∈ L¹(μ)), then E[X] is exactly the Bochner integral of X with respect to μ — the definitional unfolding of the mean operator. Second: if X is square-integrable (X ∈ L²(μ)), then (i) the centered square ω ↦ (X ω − E[X])^2 is itself μ-integrable, and (ii) Var[X] equals E[(X − E[X])^2], the expectation of that squared deviation — the definitional unfolding of the variance operator. Only claim (i), the integrability of the centered square under an L² hypothesis, carries genuine mathematical content; the two equalities hold by definition of the two local operators and in fact hold for every X, integrable or not.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The two equalities are definitionally trivial: LocalDef001 μ X is literally defined as ∫ ω, X ω ∂μ, so the first conclusion is a restatement of the definition; likewise LocalDef002 μ X is literally defined as LocalDef001 μ (fun ω ↦ (X ω − LocalDef001 μ X)^2), so the second equality is also definitionally true. Neither equality actually uses its antecedent, IsProbabilityMeasure, or any property of X.

Consequently the Integrable hypothesis in the first implication and the MemLp hypothesis in the second are strictly stronger than needed for the equalities; they are only genuinely used (and only can be used) for the integrability claim (X − E X)^2 ∈ L¹(μ).

Both local operators are total and rely on the Bochner-integral junk-value convention (integral of a non-integrable function = 0). So E[X] and Var[X] as encoded return 0 rather than being undefined for badly behaved X; the statement does not distinguish 'variance is zero' from 'variance is undefined'.

X is not assumed measurable at the binder; measurability enters only through the a.e.-strong-measurability component inside Integrable/MemLp. For a non-measurable X neither implication has a satisfiable antecedent, so both are vacuously true for such X — the statement carries no information there.

The IsProbabilityMeasure instance is required for the reading of these integrals as expectation and variance, but nothing in the encoded propositions actually depends on μ(Ω) = 1; the same statement would hold for an arbitrary measure. Its role is interpretive, not logical.

The nonnegativity of the variance, the alternative formula Var[X] = E[X²] − (E[X])², the finiteness of Var[X], and the L² ⊆ L¹ inclusion (which under a probability measure is what makes E[X] well defined in the second branch) are not stated anywhere.

The conclusion of the second implication does not assert that Var[X] is finite as a real number beyond the fact that it is a real value — finiteness is captured only indirectly by the integrability claim.

'Random variable', 'expectation' and 'variance' as probabilistic notions are not encoded semantically: nothing in the type names or the statement forces the intended interpretation; the reading depends entirely on the two local definitions and the probability-measure instance.
ambiguities: The intended names/roles of LocalDef001 and LocalDef002 are anonymized; I read them purely from their bodies as 'expectation/mean of X under μ' and 'variance of X under μ'. If they were intended to denote something else (e.g. a conditional or normalized quantity), the bodies do not support that.

It is unclear whether the definitional triviality of the two equalities is intentional (an API-level 'unfolding lemma' recording that the defined operators agree with the standard integral formulas) or whether stronger, non-definitional content was intended (e.g. Var[X] = E[X²] − (E[X])²). As stated, only the integrability conjunct has real content.
The dossier gives no information on whether an L²-implies-L¹ step or the finiteness of E[X] under the second branch was meant to be part of the claim; those do not appear in the target type.

MeasureTheory.integral's junk-value behavior is inferred from standard Mathlib convention rather than from the supplied definition body (which is opaque, `MeasureTheory.wrapped✝.1`); the vacuity/totality remarks above rest on that inference.
